home.title: CouchDesk: Free Console Mode for Your Windows PC
home.description: Turn your Windows 10/11 PC into a console: Steam, Epic, GOG and Xbox games in one library, played with an Xbox or PS5 controller or your phone. Free.
home.ogTitle: CouchDesk: your Windows PC in console mode
home.shareAlt: The CouchDesk logo and the line: your Windows PC in console mode
home.shareLine: Your Windows PC in console mode
home.h1: Console mode for your Windows PC
home.lead: CouchDesk swaps the desktop for a console screen you run with a controller, keyboard or phone. It runs on Windows 10 too, where Xbox mode can't.
home.libraryH2: All your games in the CouchDesk library
home.libraryP: CouchDesk gathers what you have installed from Steam, Epic, GOG and Xbox or Game Pass. EA, Ubisoft or Battle.net games come from the Start menu: open one and press “Mark as game”. Your apps are there too, with their real icons.
home.insideH2: Cloud, browser and emulators in CouchDesk
home.cloudH3: Xbox Cloud Gaming and PS5 Remote Play
home.cloudP: Xbox Cloud Gaming in full screen and Remote Play for your PS5 with chiaki-ng.
home.browserH3: Netflix, YouTube and DAZN in the console browser
home.browserP: 24 shortcuts: Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, HBO Max, DAZN, YouTube, Twitch, Spotify and more. Hold Esc or press the Xbox button to leave.
home.emuH3: Emulators the console installs with one button
home.emuP: They install and update themselves, with folders for games, BIOS and saves. If a new version breaks, roll back.
home.padsH2: Xbox and PlayStation controllers, or your phone, for all of Windows
home.padsCardP: Xbox, PS4 and PS5, wired or Bluetooth, all at once. The touchpad works as a mouse. Button profiles and an on-screen keyboard.
home.phoneCardP: Scan the QR code: your phone becomes a gamepad, touchpad or keyboard, and switches mode by itself.
home.dgHubAlt: CouchDesk in the middle, linked to Xbox, PS4 and PS5 controllers, the keyboard and a phone.
home.dgLanesAlt: A phone joins CouchDesk with a QR code and works as a gamepad, touchpad or keyboard across Windows.
home.roomH2: Screensaver, ambient mode, music and Claude
home.screensaverH3: A Windows screensaver with clock and weather
home.screensaverP: Time, date and weather, Apple TV style. Low power, and it can replace the Windows screensaver.
home.ambienceP: Fireplace, waterfall or rain in full screen, to leave in the background.
home.musicH3: Music on the console, by controller or voice
home.musicP: Spotify or any player: now playing, pause, next and per-app volume.
home.claudeH3: Claude, the assistant, inside the console
home.claudeP: Talk or type. Open it over a game with Ctrl+Alt+Space or View+Y.
home.exitP: From any game or app, one gesture takes you back to the CouchDesk home screen.
home.exitPadP: Press the Xbox button or the PS button.
home.exitPhoneP: Press Home on the phone controller.
home.bootH2: Turn on the PC straight into CouchDesk
home.bootLead: Switch on “Boot straight into the console” and the PC starts straight in CouchDesk.
home.bootP1: One button takes you back to the normal desktop when you need it.
home.bootP2: Sound, brightness, power and Wi-Fi all change with the controller.
home.bootP3: Animated backgrounds like the PS5, or your own image, video or 3D model. Themes with menu music.
home.diffP: What Xbox mode, Steam Big Picture and Playnite each do on their own, in one app.

faq.a: Nothing. It's free and open source under the MIT license. No account, no ads and no telemetry.

faq.q: Which Windows versions does it run on?
Windows warns me when I open the installer
faq.a: The installer isn't signed yet. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. More details.

faq.q: How do I get back to the Windows desktop?
faq.a: In CouchDesk, open Desktop and press “Go back to normal Windows mode”.

faq.q: Does CouchDesk download games or BIOS files?
faq.a: No. It never downloads games, BIOS files or keys: use the ones from your own consoles.
Spanish, English, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German and Italian. The community can add more.

download.title: Download CouchDesk for Windows 10 and 11 (free)
download.description: Download CouchDesk free for 64-bit Windows 10 and 11. Requirements, step-by-step install and what to do if SmartScreen warns you about the installer.
download.lead: Version {version} “{codename}”. Free, no account, open source. The installer is on GitHub.

list: 64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11.
An Xbox, PS4 or PS5 controller, the keyboard or your phone.
Internet only for the cloud, the browser and emulator updates.

steps: Open the latest release on GitHub and download the file ending in _x64-setup.exe.
Run it. If Windows warns you, see the section below.
When it finishes, CouchDesk opens. Connect a controller or scan the QR code with your phone.
Want it to start when you turn on the PC? Go to Settings, Startup.

blocks.p: SmartScreen warns about programs it doesn't know yet. The CouchDesk installer isn't signed yet, which is why the warning shows up.

steps: Click “More info”.
Check that the file name matches the one you downloaded from GitHub.
Click “Run anyway”.

blocks.note: Only download CouchDesk from GitHub. The code is public and anyone can review it.

blocks.p: In CouchDesk, open Desktop and press “Go back to normal Windows mode”. You can also turn it off in Settings, Startup, or uninstall it from Windows settings.

vs-xbox.title: Xbox Mode Alternative for Windows 10 and 11 | CouchDesk
vs-xbox.description: CouchDesk vs Windows 11 Xbox mode: requirements, stores, PS5 Remote Play, emulators and phone as a controller. An honest comparison.
vs-xbox.lead: Xbox mode is Microsoft's console screen for Windows 11. CouchDesk does something similar, on Windows 10 too, and adds PS5 Remote Play, emulators and your phone as a controller.

head: CouchDesk
Xbox mode
rows: Through Windows Update, in phases and select markets
Steam, Epic, GOG, Xbox and more from the Start menu
Installed games from major stores, plus Game Pass
Installed and updated with one button
Free, part of Windows, closed source

blocks.p: If you're on an up-to-date Windows 11, play mostly Game Pass and want something official from Microsoft, Xbox mode is a good choice. It ships with Windows, so there's nothing to install.

list: Your PC runs Windows 10, or Xbox mode hasn't reached your country yet.
You want to stream your PS5 or play emulators with the same controller.
You want your phone as a gamepad, touchpad or keyboard.
You want Netflix, DAZN or YouTube with a controller, without leaving the console.

blocks.p: Yes. CouchDesk opens your Xbox and Game Pass games and doesn't touch Xbox mode. Pick which one starts with the PC.

sources: Microsoft: Windows gaming full screen experience
Xbox Wire: Xbox mode comes to Windows 11 PCs

vs-bigpicture.title: Steam Big Picture Alternative for All Your Games | CouchDesk
vs-bigpicture.description: CouchDesk vs Steam Big Picture: games from every store, Xbox and PS5 cloud play, emulators and booting without the desktop. The real differences.
vs-bigpicture.lead: Big Picture is Steam's big-screen mode, and it's great for Steam. CouchDesk brings all your stores together and also runs Windows with a controller.

head: CouchDesk
Steam Big Picture
rows: Yes, with store, achievements and friends
Epic, GOG, Xbox and other stores
Only if you add them by hand as non-Steam games
Xbox Cloud Gaming and PS5 Remote Play
Installed and updated with one button
Opens Steam in Big Picture at sign-in, on top of the desktop

blocks.p: If nearly everything you play is on Steam, Big Picture is the easiest choice. Steam Input sets up any controller game by game, and you get the store, chat and achievements.

list: You have games on Epic, GOG, Xbox, EA or Ubisoft as well as Steam.
You want Xbox cloud, your PS5 remotely and emulators in one place.
You want the PC to start in the console, not on the desktop.

blocks.p: Yes. CouchDesk lists your Steam games and launches them through Steam, so Steam Input keeps working in them.

vs-playnite.title: CouchDesk vs Playnite: Which Console Mode Fits You?
vs-playnite.description: CouchDesk vs Playnite and its fullscreen mode: library, emulators, cloud play, Windows settings and phone as a controller. An honest comparison.
vs-playnite.lead: Playnite is the best-known open-source library manager for Windows, and nobody organises games better. CouchDesk is less configurable, but it works as a whole console.

head: CouchDesk
Playnite
rows: Steam, Epic, GOG, Xbox and more from the Start menu
Very rich: descriptions, tags, play time
Its own themes and Claude extensions
A large community of add-ons and themes
Installed, updated and rolled back with one button
Detects and imports the ones you have
Xbox Cloud Gaming and PS5 Remote Play

blocks.p: If you like to sort, tag and customise everything, Playnite has no equal. Its community of add-ons and themes is huge, built over years of development.

list: You want the living-room PC to work like a console, without the desktop.
You want Xbox and PS5 cloud play, emulators and streaming in one menu.
You'd rather have something that works right after install, with little setup.

guide-boot.title: Boot Windows Straight into Console Mode
guide-boot.description: How to make a Windows 10 or 11 PC start on a console screen instead of the desktop, and how to undo it. A step-by-step guide.
guide-boot.h1: Boot Windows straight into console mode
guide-boot.lead: Turn on the PC and the console appears, not the desktop. Here's how to set it up with CouchDesk, and how to undo it.

blocks.p: Windows opens the desktop (File Explorer) when you sign in. CouchDesk can take its place, for your user only. With no desktop behind it, the PC uses less memory.

steps: Install CouchDesk from the download page.
Open Settings and go to Startup.
Turn on “Boot straight into the console”.
Restart the PC. After you sign in, you'll see CouchDesk.

blocks.note: To start without a password, set up Windows automatic sign-in. Only do this on a home PC.

blocks.h2: How to get back to the desktop

list: For a while: open Desktop inside CouchDesk.
For good: Settings, Startup, and turn the setting off. Or press “Go back to normal Windows mode”.
If something goes wrong, uninstall CouchDesk: the normal startup comes back.

blocks.p: Windows 11 Xbox mode can also start in full screen, but it needs Windows 11 24H2 or later. CouchDesk does it on Windows 10 too. See the comparison.

guide-remoteplay.title: PS5 Remote Play on PC with a Controller (chiaki-ng)
guide-remoteplay.description: Play your PS5 from a Windows PC with a controller, using chiaki-ng inside CouchDesk. Requirements, first connection and tips for a smooth stream.
guide-remoteplay.menuSub: Your PS5 on the living-room TV
guide-remoteplay.h1: PS5 Remote Play on PC, with a controller
guide-remoteplay.lead: Play your PS5 from another room, on the PC hooked up to the TV. CouchDesk uses chiaki-ng, an open-source Remote Play client.

list: A PS5 with Remote Play turned on: Settings, System, Remote Play.
Your PlayStation Network account.
The PC and the PS5 on the same network. Wired is best, or 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
A PS5, PS4 or Xbox controller on the PC.

steps: In CouchDesk, open Cloud and choose PS5 Remote Play.
If chiaki-ng isn't there, CouchDesk installs it with one button.
The first time, pair the console with your account and the code the PS5 shows.
Pick your PS5 in the list and play. To go back, press the Xbox or PS button.

list: Connect the PS5 with a network cable if you can.
Drop to 1080p if you see stutter.
Pause big downloads while you play.

blocks.note: chiaki-ng is an independent project and is not made by Sony.

guide-controller.title: Use a PS5 or PS4 Controller on PC Without Drivers
guide-controller.description: Connect a DualSense or DualShock 4 to Windows by cable or Bluetooth and use it without drivers in CouchDesk: menus, touchpad as mouse and keyboard.
guide-controller.crumb: PS5 and PS4 controller on PC
guide-controller.menu: PS5 and PS4 controller, no drivers
guide-controller.h1: Your PS5 or PS4 controller on PC, no drivers
guide-controller.lead: CouchDesk reads the DualSense and DualShock 4 straight from Windows. You don't need DS4Windows or any other program.

blocks.p: Wired: plug it in over USB and you're done.

steps: In Windows, open Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Add device.
On the controller, hold PS and Create (PS5) or PS and Share (PS4) until the light flashes.
Pick the controller in the Windows list.

blocks.h2: What you can do with it

list: Move through every CouchDesk menu.
Use the touchpad as a mouse: one finger moves, two scroll, press to click.
Press OPTIONS + SHARE to switch between controller, mouse and keyboard across Windows.
Press the PS button to go back to CouchDesk.
Connect several controllers at once and make button profiles.

blocks.p: CouchDesk doesn't turn the controller into an Xbox one. Many PC games already support the DualSense. On Steam, Steam Input handles the rest.

guide-emulators.title: Emulators on Windows, Run with a Controller
guide-emulators.description: Install and update emulators on Windows with one button and play with a controller: game, BIOS and save folders, and rollback to the previous version.
guide-emulators.h1: Emulators on Windows, run with a controller
guide-emulators.lead: CouchDesk installs emulators, keeps them up to date and puts their folders at hand. All from the couch.

blocks.p: DuckStation (PlayStation), PCSX2 (PS2), RPCS3 (PS3), shadPS4 (PS4), Dolphin (GameCube and Wii), ares (Nintendo 64), melonDS (Nintendo DS) and others. Each one shows how well it will run on your PC.

steps: Open Emulators and pick one.
Press Install. CouchDesk downloads the official release.
When there's a new version, it updates. If it breaks, press “Previous version”.

blocks.p: Each emulator has three folders: games, BIOS and saves. To fill them:

list: “Bring in” copies from a USB stick or any folder on the PC.
From your phone or another PC: scan the QR code and drag the files into the browser.
Over FTP or LocalSend on your home network.

blocks.note: CouchDesk never downloads games, BIOS files or keys. Use copies from your own consoles and games.
